column1: # JSON SCHEMA IMPORT -- JSON Schema 2020-12 in, aontu text out (G12).
# `src` is the schema's JSON text; `expect` is the report: the aontu
# text, the `lossy` list of keywords a later phase carries, the
# `verdict`, and `errors` (code, class, path and sites; the message and
# hint are prose) when the text is not a schema. An `opts` key holds the
# run's options: `defaults`, the entry's retrieval `uri`, and the
# `documents` a reference may reach, by URI, whose sites name that URI.
# The importer owns the meaning of every keyword it carries (ADR-047): a
# schema object splits by kind, numbers are written by value in the leaf
# that value selects, objects take optional keys and guarded spreads,
# arrays one list spread guarded by index, and a `$ref` an alias where
# the root is a map, whose declaration keeps the schema's identity in
# EVERY EXPECTATION HERE WAS OBTAINED BY RUNNING BOTH ENGINES AND
# REQUIRING THEM TO AGREE, never by copying one engine's answer. The
# conformance of the whole is the vendored suite's job
# Booleans, the empty schema and the kinds.
# Numbers are written by value, in the leaf the value selects.

column4: {"aontu":"null|boolean|number|empty()|map|list\\n","lossy":[{"construct":"minimum","path":"#/minimum","reason":"the number 1e5000 exceeds the exactness budget, so the keyword is dropped"}],"verdict":"lossy"}

column1: # A position whose meet is bottom admits nothing, and is nil.
# anyOf is | where at most one branch can survive, a count otherwise.

column4: {"aontu":"nof(\\n  min(1),\\n  null|boolean|number|empty()|{ a:any }|list,\\n  null|boolean|number|empty()|{ b:any }|list\\n) & map\\n","lossy":[],"verdict":"ok"}

column1: # oneOf is a count of exactly one, or | over distinct scalar literals.
# not is a count of none; beside one string or integer type, an excluded enum is neq.
# if pairs with the then and else of its own object, as when; either alone asserts nothing.
# dependentSchemas and dependentRequired are conditionals on a key being present.
# contains counts the items its schema admits; uniqueItems is unique().
# Annotations ride the value in a meta() record, deprecated as deprecate(); a default is no preference unless asked.

column4: {"aontu":"meta(\\n  null|boolean|number|meta(empty(), {\\n    contentEncoding: \\"base64\\"\\n    contentMediaType: \\"text/plain\\"\\n    contentSchema: type: \\"string\\"\\n  })|map|list,\\n  {\\n    comment: \\"c\\"\\n    default: \\"a\\"\\n    examples: [\\"a\\"]\\n    format: \\"email\\"\\n    readOnly: true\\n    writeOnly: false\\n  }\\n)\\n","lossy":[],"verdict":"ok"}

column1: # Text that is not a schema.
# A count past int64 keeps its digits, and a subschema nothing references is
# still checked: one written wrongly fails the import as a referenced one does.
# A string property beside two spreads imports as written: the meet with
# each spread lets the spread's disjunction drive, where `empty()` once
# refused it and the whole schema imported as `nil`.

column4: {"aontu":"a?: empty()\\n&: match(key(0), re(\\"^x\\"), number, any)\\n&: match(key(0), re(\\"^y\\"), boolean, any)\\n","lossy":[],"verdict":"ok"}

column1: # An object root keeps its aliases when it also carries annotations, a

# whose object branch carries a count beside a dependency.
